title: Zero-based list indexing

curriculum.title: Zero-Based List Indexing in Python
curriculum.answer:
## Zero-based list indexing

### Concept introduction
A list keeps items in order, and each order place has a number called an index. In Python the order starts at `0`, so the first item is at place `0` and the next item is at place `1`. You read one item with `name[place]`.

### How it works
A list variable names the whole ordered group. Writing square brackets with a non-negative whole number after the variable selects exactly one stored item. The number is the position counted from zero, not from one. So `colors[0]` is the first item and `colors[1]` is the second item.

```python
colors = ["red", "green", "blue"]
print(colors[0])
print(colors[1])
```

```text
red
green
```

The program first creates `colors` with three items. Then `colors[0]` looks at position `0` and supplies `"red"`. Next `colors[1]` looks at position `1` and supplies `"green"`. Each indexed read returns one item, while `colors` still holds the whole list.

The index must name an existing position in that supplied nonempty list. A three-item list has valid non-negative positions `0`, `1`, and `2` only. The last position is therefore different from the number of items.

```python
students = ["Hermione", "Harry", "Ron"]
first = students[0]
second = students[1]
third = students[2]
print(first)
print(second)
print(third)
```

```text
Hermione
Harry
Ron
```

Here `first`, `second`, and `third` are new variables. Each assignment binds a new name to the selected item from `students`. The original list is unchanged.

### Common mistakes
New programmers often read `students[1]` as the first student. It is the second because counting starts at zero. Another mistake is expecting `students[0]` to return the whole list. It returns only the item at position `0`.

units.explanation: Non-negative positions start at 0, so select existing positions directly from the supplied list and store the result without changing the input.
units.opening_question: If a list holds three names in order, how do you read only the first one?
